<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Attach a resource and learn the two kinds of name used in a session.
</div>

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from [Getting started](book-00-start.html).
**You need:** the packages and the matching practice connection described in
[Before you start](book-00-start.html#before-you-start).
Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed
with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

## Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the `book-work` directory created in
[Getting started](book-00-start.html#get-the-book-helpers). Run this setup first:


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"
```

The `site` connection is ready. The shared `connection.R` selects DSLite or Opal and resolves the resource names.

## One connection list

A *connection* is a logged-in session. Our DSLite helper made one, named `site`.


``` r
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"
```

Most calls accept `conns`. Passing it explicitly makes clear where a request goes.

## The Opal login path

Edit `tools/book/connection.R` once to set `book_driver <- "Opal"`, your
`opal_url`, `opal_project`, `opal_resources` and `opal_profile`. Keep credentials in
`BOOK_OPAL_USER` and `BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD` in your local environment. Restart R and
run the setup above. Every public practice chapter uses that same file.

`book_connect()` logs in with DSOpal when Opal is selected; with DSLite it calls
`book_practice()` locally. Both return a list, so the assignment
`conns <- practice$conns` is essential. Questionnaire chapters use their explicitly
separate local fixture. The optional [administrator walkthrough](book-00-start.html#use-the-same-two-resources-on-opal)
creates and checks both Opal resources.


``` r
resource_names
```

```
#>   gibleed   numeric 
#> "gibleed" "numeric"
```

These are the names used by every attach and switch below. With Opal they include
the configured project prefix, even when you rename either resource.

## A resource is a route to a database

A *resource* stores the connection details on the server. On the practice server its name
is `gibleed`. In the optional Opal setup it is `practice.gibleed`.

A *symbol* is an R object name inside the DataSHIELD session. Attach the resource
and deliberately name the session handle `omop`:


``` r
ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = resource_names[["gibleed"]], symbol = "omop", conns = conns)
```

The server opens its database connection. This does not copy the database into R
on your laptop. The shared configuration supplies the correct resource name for either driver.

ds.omop.columns("person", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$site

Subsequent calls can omit `symbol` because its default is `omop`. An output symbol
such as `D_people` is different: it names a table built later by a recipe.

## End a session deliberately

At the end of your own work, call `ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)` and then
`DSI::datashield.logout(conns)`. Start again with the practice helper for another
chapter. The reproduction script performs both cleanup calls after each chapter.

## Switch between the two practice resources

The same practice server also offers the numeric Synthea27Nj database. Disconnect
the current OMOP handle, then attach that resource on the same login connection:


``` r
ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
numeric_session <- ds.omop.connect(resource = resource_names[["numeric"]], conns = conns)
class(numeric_session)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_session"
```

This changes the database behind the OMOP handle. It does not copy or combine
patient rows between resources. On Opal the corresponding name is `practice.numeric`.
Return to GiBleed for the next introductory chapters:


``` r
ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
session <- ds.omop.connect(resource = resource_names[["gibleed"]], conns = conns)
class(session)
```

```
#> [1] "omop_session"
```

The numeric chapters will open their own fresh `numeric` session. Keeping resource
selection explicit prevents accidentally running a lab recipe against GiBleed's
empty numeric-value fields.

## Exercise 2: a common variant

Resolve resource names for an Opal project called teaching. Do you need to reconnect for this local calculation?

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
book_resource_names("Opal", "teaching", c(gibleed = "bleeding", numeric = "labs"))
```

```
#>             gibleed             numeric 
#> "teaching.bleeding"     "teaching.labs"
```

No. Name resolution is local; attaching the resolved resource is a separate server operation.

</details>

## Exercise 3: a pitfall to avoid

Use an explicit handle for a different table, then verify the current server version.

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
knitr::kable(ds.omop.columns("death", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$site)
```



|column_name             |cdm_datatype |db_datatype |concept_role      |semantic_class |fk_domain    |is_date |is_extension |is_untyped_identifier |is_sensitive |is_blocked |is_quasi_identifier |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:-----------|:-----------------|:--------------|:------------|:-------|:------------|:---------------------|:------------|:----------|:-------------------|
|person_id               |integer      |real        |non_concept       |ordinary       |             |FALSE   |FALSE        |FALSE                 |FALSE        |FALSE      |FALSE               |
|death_date              |date         |text        |non_concept       |ordinary       |             |TRUE    |FALSE        |FALSE                 |FALSE        |FALSE      |TRUE                |
|death_datetime          |datetime     |text        |non_concept       |ordinary       |             |TRUE    |FALSE        |FALSE                 |FALSE        |FALSE      |TRUE                |
|death_type_concept_id   |integer      |real        |type_concept      |concept        |Type Concept |FALSE   |FALSE        |FALSE                 |FALSE        |FALSE      |FALSE               |
|cause_concept_id        |integer      |real        |attribute_concept |concept        |             |FALSE   |FALSE        |FALSE                 |FALSE        |FALSE      |FALSE               |
|cause_source_value      |varchar(50)  |text        |non_concept       |ordinary       |             |FALSE   |FALSE        |FALSE                 |TRUE         |TRUE       |FALSE               |
|cause_source_concept_id |integer      |real        |source_concept    |concept        |             |FALSE   |FALSE        |FALSE                 |TRUE         |TRUE       |FALSE               |

``` r
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)[c("server", "published", "running", "ready")]
```

```
#>   server published running ready
#> 1   site    2.10.5  2.10.5  TRUE
```

The same handle routes both calls to the current resource. A symbol name does not describe which dataset it contains.

</details>
## Recap

The resource identifies a database; `omop` is its session handle; `D_people` will name a private result.
